subject: art-design
source_note: Topic structure follows the Eduqas/WJEC A-Level Art and Design specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships.

units.name: Component 1: Personal Investigation
units.blurb: Practical enquiry plus an extended personal study

units.name: Endorsed Titles & Areas of Study
units.blurb: The disciplines a student may specialise in

topics.name: Investigation & Research
topics.blurb: Critical investigation of sources, artists and contexts (AO1)

topics.name: Development & Experimentation
topics.blurb: Refining ideas through media and processes (AO2)

topics.name: Personal Study (Essay)
topics.blurb: 1000-3000 word continuous written study with critical analysis

topics.name: ESA Preparatory Work
topics.blurb: Sustained preparatory studies from the set theme

topics.name: ESA Final Outcome
topics.blurb: Outcome produced under 15 hours of sustained focus

topics.name: Fine Art
topics.blurb: Aesthetic and conceptual practice across painting, sculpture, lens media

topics.name: Textile Design
topics.blurb: Constructed, printed and stitched textiles and fashion

topics.name: Three-Dimensional Design
topics.blurb: Product, spatial, architectural and ceramic design

topics.name: Photography
topics.blurb: Lens- and light-based image making, still and moving

topics.name: Critical & Contextual Studies
topics.blurb: Critical analysis and appraisal of artists and movements

connections.why: Critical research drives the development of personal ideas
Experimentation is recorded and reflected upon as work progresses
Documented development resolves into a personal outcome
The same critical investigation underpins the extended written personal study
The written study contextualises and informs the practical outcome
Independence built in the personal investigation prepares for the set assignment
Preparatory studies culminate in the sustained-focus outcome
Critical and contextual study directly supports the analytical personal study
Each endorsed title is realised through the same development process
Photographic image-making often feeds graphic communication
Material-led making links textile and three-dimensional design
Investigation skills are the foundation of critical and contextual studies
